heading: INT. MARLOW FARMHOUSE - KITCHEN - EARLY MORNING

units.text: INT. MARLOW FARMHOUSE - KITCHEN - EARLY MORNING
A cold stove.
A table with three mismatched chairs.
A single teacup, unwashed, on the sill.
CONSTANCE, 40s, stands at the sink with her coat still buttoned.
She does not turn on the tap.
Her sister HATTIE, 30s, enters from the hall in a nightgown and bare feet, hugging her elbows.
At the table, WALTER, 70s, their father, sits upright in his Sunday collar, a folded newspaper in front of him that he has not opened.
She watches the back of her sister's head.
She says nothing.
Hattie crosses to the stove, strikes a match, and stands holding it until the flame reaches her fingers.
You'll burn yourself.
units.name: CONSTANCE

units.text: I know.
units.name: HATTIE

units.text: She shakes it out.
The smoke curls toward the ceiling.
Sit down, both of you.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Neither sits.
Constance finally turns on the tap, and the water runs over a plate she isn't washing.
She came back last night.
units.name: HATTIE

units.text: Who did?
units.name: CONSTANCE

units.text: You know who.
units.name: HATTIE

units.text: Walter unfolds the paper, folds it again, smoother this time.
He sets it square on the table.
Your mother is in the churchyard. We buried her Tuesday.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: She does not look at him.
She keeps her eyes on her sister's hands, shaking now, the matchbox rattling in them.
Hattie slides it across the counter, away from herself, toward the sink.
Take that outside.
units.name: CONSTANCE

units.text: Why?
units.name: HATTIE

units.text: Because Father is looking at it.
units.name: CONSTANCE

units.text: Walter is.
He is looking at the matchbox as if it were an animal.
Slowly he reaches out and lays his big, spotted hand over it.
Neither daughter moves.
Outside, a rooster crows, late.
